messages:
kai: FYI — after landing the RoPE scaling tweak for Mixtral yesterday we're seeing a ~15-20% p95 p99 latency increase on short chat prompts (<=64 tokens). low churn but consistent across our hosted fleet. repro & quick profile below.

matt: ugh. do we know if this is kernel selection or batching window interactions?

kai: initial flamegraphs point at attention kernels + KV copy. looks like attention_fwd kernel time up ~30% and KV cache maintenance (copy/shift) up ~2-3x for short seqs. p95 jump mostly on single-request path; throughput steady.

anna: can you paste the profile and the exact model config you rolled?

kai: sure — profile snippet:
```
Mixtral-8B | short_prompt (<=64) | p95 182ms -> 217ms after change
Top kernels by time:
- attention_fwd (fused) : 42% -> 55%
- kv_shift / kv_copy     : 8% -> 22%
- softmax               : 6% -> 7%
- other                : remaining
Config diff: rop_scaling = "dynamic_base_v2" (was "legacy_scale"), use_fused_attention=true, kernel_selector=auto
```

lin: interesting. could tokenization be inflating token counts causing more KV ops? any byte-fallback on these prompts?

kai: good catch — we also rolled in a tokenizer patch that changes byte-fallback heuristics for rare unicode. a few of the failing prompts show token_count +10-30% (multilingual chat) which would exacerbate KV costs. example:
```
original text: "Bonjour — j'ai un problème"
old tokens: 8
new tokens: 11 (byte-fallback on apostrophe variants)
```

matt: so two simultaneous changes (RoPE scaling + tokenizer) — noisy signal. which one explains attention kernel time increase?

kai: I bisected. when I revert tokenizer -> token counts go back and p95 drops ~6-7% but not all the way. reverting RoPE_scaling alone drops p95 ~12-13% by restoring smaller rotary angles on short seqs. both together explain the whole delta.

anna: that suggests RoPE scaling increased per-token computation (maybe different kernel path or worse cache locality) while tokenizer increased token volume. we should treat as two fixes: immediate rollback of tokenizer change for hosted Mixtral traffic and longer-term tune RoPE heuristics.

lin: for the RoPE piece, could this trigger a different attention kernel in the selector? kernel_selector=auto might pick the slow path if head dims or seq len cross thresholds. what's mixtral head/kv dims in the runtime config?

kai: Mixtral 8B config: heads=32, kv_dim=64, head_dim=128? (we store head/kvdim in runtime meta). The new scaling modifies rotary base which changes effective sin/cos precomputation shape for short seqs. I suspect the selector thinks this maps poorly to the fast fused kernel for short sequences and picks the generic kernel.

matt: check kernel selector logs: enable `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_selector` on a small pool; grep for `chosen_kernel` and `reason`. Also try forcing `kernel_selector=static_small_seq` to see if fused path regains perf.

kai: did that: forcing `static_small_seq` restores attention_fwd time but KV copy stays higher because of token count + KV packing change.

lin: ok, actions: (1) rollback tokenizer byte-fallback change for Mixtral traffic (hosted) — quick, low-risk. (2) add kernel_selector debug and run A/B forcing small_seq fused kernel to confirm hypothesis. (3) if fused kernel helps, we need a selector rule that maps rop_scaling variants to preferred kernel.

anna: for (3) we should add a cheap selector heuristic: if model == mixtral && rop_scaling in [dynamic_base_v2] && seq_len <= 128 -> prefer fused_smallseq. That avoids blanket static changes.

kai: agreed. also note KV cache behavior: switching tokenization changed special token insertion (BOS/EOS handling) -> some prompts now include an extra BOS leading to extra KV writes per request and more frequent KV compactions in the batcher. small snippet from our KV metrics:
```
kv.entries_written_per_request: 64 -> 78
kv.compaction_calls_per_min: 4 -> 18
```

matt: compaction thrash would definitely spike p95. can we change batcher to prefer coalescing by initial seq len and avoid compactions inside the small windows? maybe set `batch_window_ms=6` -> `4` or disable compaction for short-lived requests.

kai: lowering batch_window helps latency but increases CPU overhead; short-term I'd prefer the tokenizer rollback + selector tweak.

lin: also worth checking RoPE scaling math for odd head dims/kv dims — if the sine/cos arrays no longer align to 32/64 boundaries we lose vectorization and pay. confirm memalign in precompute.

kai: yeah I saw unaligned sin_cos buffers in the allocator logs after the change. will add padding to round to 64 bytes and see.

anna: can someone put a small repro harness in /infra/perf that runs Mixtral short prompts with both tokenizer versions and rop variants and dumps `nvprof`/lightweight flame + kernel_selector logs? mark as `perf/regressions/mixtral-rope-<ts>`.

kai: I'll drop a quick script tonight. example run command I'm using:
```bash
# run 20 qps for 60s, collect kernel selector + kv metrics
RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_selector,kv RUNTIME_OVERRIDE_MODEL=mixtral-8b ./bin/run_infer --prompt-file short_prompts.txt --qps 20 --dur 60 --collect-flame
```

matt: nice. owners: kai -> triage & script, lin -> kernel selector patch & alignment, anna -> coordinate rollback for tokenizer on hosted. dev-bot: create rollout ticket?

dev-bot: Ticket created: INF-2137 "Mixtral RoPE/tokenizer regression investigation" assigned to kai, lin, anna. :white_check_mark:

kai: will post perf diffs in the ticket and attach flamegraphs. plan: rollback tokenizer for hosted Mixtral within 2h, run A/B with selector tweak, then consider safe rollout of RoPE tweak after adding selector rule + alignment patch.

anna: thanks — tag me once rollback is done and we have numbers. :thumbsup:

lin: also add a unit test in kernel selector that simulates head_dim/kvdim combos and ensures we don't flip kernels for minor rop param changes.

kai: noted. I'll keep thread updated.

matt: thanks all — good catch catching tokenizer interaction early.
